facts.text: Jefferson sits where the Rock and Crawfish rivers meet, a spot chosen for water power and steamboat navigation in the 1830s.
The city’s founders were New England farmers who brought Yankee values, including a passion for education and abolitionism, to the frontier.
Jefferson’s historic downtown preserves buildings on the National Register, reflecting its 19th‑century commercial boom.
The 1911 Carnegie library, now a performing‑arts hub, showcases Prairie School architecture and the town’s early commitment to learning.
Camp Jefferson, a World War II German POW camp, once stood on the county fairgrounds, a reminder of the city’s wartime role.
Gemütlichkeit Days, started in 1971, celebrates the German heritage that many Jefferson residents share, echoing the town’s immigrant roots.
